title: Electricity, heat, and operating costs
outcome: Calculate energy consumption and operating cost from measured or provided inputs.
show: Make an operating sheet with wall power, hours, energy, price per kWh, cooling and other costs.
concepts: Watts measure power. Divide watts by 1,000 to get kilowatts. Multiply kilowatts by elapsed hours to get kilowatt-hours.
Joules per terahash describes the energy required for a given amount of hashing. Evaluate cooling power, uptime, and measurement conditions alongside miner efficiency.
Electricity cost is one input. Hardware, cooling, downtime, network difficulty, pool fees and payout rules also affect outcomes. A profitability claim needs a stated period and inputs.
replicate: Use a sample miner drawing 800 W for eight hours at $0.12 per kWh. Compute energy and electricity cost.
Add hypothetical cooling power of 200 W for the same eight hours and recompute both figures.
check: What is the total with cooling in that example?
Total power is 1 kW, energy is 8 kWh, and electricity costs $0.96.

challenge.title: Fit the run inside the power budget
challenge.prompt: A practice rig draws 800 W. Run it for at least 6 hours and spend at most $0.60 at $0.12/kWh.
challenge.tip: Divide watts by 1,000 to get kW. Multiply by hours to get kWh, then multiply by the price per kWh.
